newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait, Saudi may boost Neutral Zone output-report.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait, Saudi may boost Neutral Zone output-report.

text.p: Kuwait and Saudi Arabia are considering a plan to boost onshore production in the Neutral Zone to 420,000 barrels per day (bpd) by 2005 from a current 230,000 bpd, a newspaper reported.

After the conclusion of a previously-announced project to increase production to 300,000 bpd by the year 1998 there could be "a plan to make the joint operations production reach 420,000 bpd by the year 2005," al-Watan newspaper quoted "well-placed" sources as saying.
In October the two Arab Gulf states and Saudi Arabian Texaco have agreed to spend $400 million to raise onshore output in the Neutral Zone to 300,000 bpd.
Kuwait and Riyadh have equally shared mineral rights in the zone since its establishment in 1922. The zone is operated jointly by Texaco and state-owned Kuwait Oil Company.
Japan's Arabian Oil Co Ltd operates offshore fields in the zone and plans to raise output to 350,000 bpd by the end of the century from 315,000 bpd.
